t: if he died without offspring. He died without having had sons or daughters.

and by Torah law he need not betroth his yevamah, for she is his wife, whom Heaven gave him. By Torah law there is no need for the act of betrothal, since she is already acquired to him by force of the Torah commandment. However, the Sages enacted betrothal for a yevamah (see below 2:1).
and her ketubah is on the estate of her husband who died. The ketubah is collected from the estate of her deceased husband (below 2:2).
he did not wish to perform yibbum or she did not wish. For details when there are several brothers see below 2:7-13.
and the mitzvah of yibbum takes precedence over the mitzvah of chalitzah. The mitzvah of yibbum is preferred over chalitzah.
a mamzer. One born of forbidden incestuous relations, who is forbidden to enter the congregation and to marry a Jewish woman (Hilchot Issurei Bi'ah 15:1).
one who worships idols. Who is considered a gentile for certain matters of halachah (see Hilchot Shabbat 30:15).
and as if they do not exist. As if they do not exist at all, and are not considered his children for any Torah law.
she will be her master's. The children are attributed to their mother the maidservant, and so they are slaves.
and regarding a gentile woman he says. In the warning not to marry her.

"for he will turn your son away from following Me" - he turns him away from being counted in the congregation. One who transgresses the prohibition "you shall not intermarry with them" and marries a gentile woman causes his children not to be counted in the congregation of the Lord - among Israel.
whose son was freed. A slave who is freed becomes like a convert joining the people of Israel for every matter (Hilchot Issurei Bi'ah 13:12).
they are like other converts and freed slaves. Who are considered "like a newborn child," and any family relationship they had before they converted is void (ibid. 14:11).
for he has already freed him. His status is that of a freed slave (and see further Hilchot Gerushin 10:19).
whose months were completed. Who was born at the end of his development, after nine full months of pregnancy, and there is no longer a doubt that it might be a stillborn.
a viable offspring. One made to live.
his mother performs chalitzah by rabbinic enactment and does not enter yibbum. For the Sages decreed out of concern that it might have been a stillborn, and did not exempt his mother.

once his head and most of him emerged into the world before his brother died. That his head or most of his body emerged from his mother's womb, at which point he is considered born. For if he was born after his brother's death, he does not obligate yibbum (below 6:16).
binds. Ties and obligates (a special term for the bond of the mitzvah of yibbum).
he is not his brother for any purpose. He is not considered his brother for any matter (as above halachah 4).
his birth in holiness. Who was born after the mother converted or was freed.
his conception was not in holiness. Whether the mother conceived while she was a gentile.

are considered brothers only for mourning and for testimony. The Sages enacted that for these matters they are like brothers from the father: a person mourns for his maternal brother who died (Hilchot Avel 2:1), and one may not testify in a case of his maternal brother or join with him in testimony (Hilchot Edut 13:1).
regarding inheritance. For a person does not inherit his maternal brother (Hilchot Nachalot 1:6).
brotherhood. Fraternal ties.
and they are like strangers to one another. For family ties are void upon conversion (see above halachah 4).
exempts the others. From yibbum or chalitzah, and they are permitted to marry another.
the co-wives. The other wives of the brother.
fit for the priesthood. Women whom a priest may marry (see Hilchot Issurei Bi'ah chapters 17-19).

so that she not be disqualified... by chalitzah. And she will be able to marry a priest like a widow. A woman who has performed chalitzah is forbidden to marry a priest by rabbinic enactment, because she resembles a divorcee (Hilchot Ishut 1:7, Hilchot Issurei Bi'ah 17:7).
if he is able to perform yibbum with all of them. That he can provide for their needs (see Hilchot Ishut 14:3).
from each house. From each of the brothers who died.
the one who marries. Who takes in marriage.

and a prohibition that comes from a general positive commandment, etc.. This prohibition is derived from the framework of a positive commandment, and so it is not counted as a negative prohibition but as a positive commandment.
by rabbinic enactment, like secondary relations. They are forbidden like relatives forbidden by rabbinic enactment (see Hilchot Ishut 1:6).
the prohibition of a forbidden relation was lifted. The prohibition of incest of a brother's wife was annulled (Hilchot Issurei Bi'ah 2:1).
therefore betrothal takes effect with them, like secondary relations. Unlike incestuous relations forbidden by the Torah, where betrothal is not valid (Hilchot Ishut 4:12).
like his wife whom he divorced. Whose relatives remain forbidden to him even if he divorced her (for details see Hilchot Issurei Bi'ah 2:7), and chalitzah is like divorce.
his yevamah died while still bound to him. She died without having been taken in yibbum or having performed chalitzah.
and a man may marry the sister of his chalutzah's co-wife. For relatives of a brother's wife with whom no act was done are not forbidden to him.
as we have explained. Above halachot 12-13.
if he wishes to take her back, he may take her back. And she is not considered his brother's wife outside the mitzvah of yibbum, which would be forbidden to him.
we have already explained in Hilchot Ishut. 11:3.
from the tradition. A halachic tradition.
until he grows up and is examined. Until he grows and is thirteen years and one day old, and is examined to see whether he has shown signs of adulthood (Hilchot Ishut 2:10).
for "man" is written in the passage regarding chalitzah. "And if the man does not wish to take his brother's wife" (Deuteronomy 25:7), and the word "man" means an adult.
permitted. Permitted.
after he grows up. And he will give her a get.
as will be explained. Below 5:18-21.
the minor. A girl under twelve or one who has not shown signs of adulthood (Hilchot Ishut 2:1, 3).

even if she had relations after twelve years. Where her marriage was by rabbinic enactment and she had relations after reaching twelve, we assume she is an adult and can no longer refuse (see Hilchot Gerushin 11:4). But regarding chalitzah we do not rely on the presumption of age without examination.
they grow up together. For he cannot divorce her until he grows up.

she must wait ninety days... like all other women. The Sages enacted that a woman may not remarry until ninety days after being widowed or divorced, to determine whether she is pregnant (see Hilchot Gerushin 11:18). Because of this enactment she is not eligible for yibbum during that time.
goes up to yibbum. Is permitted for yibbum.
since she is not pregnant. It became clear that she was not pregnant.
she is as if she had never performed chalitzah with him. As if no chalitzah was done at all, for she is not bound to him, since it became clear that her husband had offspring.
who did not live thirty days after birth. Who is considered a stillborn and does not exempt from yibbum (above halachah 5).

her co-wife may not marry until this one gives birth, etc.. For chalitzah and yibbum are not effective for a pregnant woman. If she gives birth to a viable child, it will be clear that they were never bound to yibbum, but the child does not exempt them until it is born.
they separate them. They keep them apart until it is clarified whether she is forbidden to him.
he may return and establish her. He may return and have relations after she miscarries, and then the yibbum takes effect properly.

he divorces her with a get and performs chalitzah for her. A get is needed because she appeared to be his wife from the time he took her in, and chalitzah because perhaps this child does not exempt her, and she is bound to yibbum (Maggid Mishneh; above halachah 5).
a forbidden relation to him. That she is his brother's wife who is not bound to yibbum.
a doubt whether he was a nine-month child of the first or a seven-month child of the last. A doubt whether he was born from the first husband who died or from the yavam.
therefore he divorces with a get. For if the child is the first husband's, she is forbidden to the yavam as a brother's wife, which is permitted only when there are no offspring.
doubtful mamzerim. Perhaps there was no obligation of yibbum there.
by rabbinic enactment... that he betroth her. By enactment of the Sages, since by Torah law he need not betroth her, for she is acquired by relations (above 1:1).
with a perutah or the worth of a perutah. As in betrothal with money (Hilchot Ishut 3:1).
as will be explained. Below 5:2, 6:18, and see Hilchot Nedarim 11:23-24.
without her knowledge. Not with her consent, which is not permitted in ordinary betrothal (Hilchot Ishut 4:1).
and a minor from betrothal. Who was betrothed to his deceased brother but not yet married, so she is still in her father's domain and can be betrothed only with his consent (ibid. 3:11-12).
the marriage blessing. The seven blessings the Sages enacted to be recited at marriage (for details see Hilchot Ishut 10:3-5).
and writes her ketubah. And the lien is on the estate of the deceased (above 1:1; for the text of this ketubah see below 4:32).
has made a complete acquisition. Since by Torah law he need not betroth her (above 1:1).
lashes for rebelliousness. Rabbinic lashes for violating the Sages' enactment that he must betroth the yevamah (and see Hilchot Ishut 3:21).
in an unnatural manner. Relations through the rectum, from behind.
the one who begins. The start of intercourse (see Hilchot Issurei Bi'ah 1:10).
the one who completes. The completion of intercourse (see ibid.).
who is not aware of anything. Who is not aware of his actions.
to thrust. An expression for a sexual act.
who was taken in yibbum, etc.. Who took her in yibbum and afterward divorced her.
and she said... I did not have relations. And according to her claim she is bound to yibbum or chalitzah.
we compel him to perform chalitzah for her, etc.. Since he has already divorced her with a get and is forbidden to perform yibbum with her (see below 5:1).
and he divorces with a get. For we suspect he may have had relations with her, and she needs a get from him.

we ask him to perform chalitzah for her. We do not compel him, since after thirty days we assume he had relations with her (Babylonian Talmud, Yevamot 111b) and chalitzah is no longer needed, but we ask him to perform chalitzah because she has forbidden herself.
she says: I had relations, etc.. Even within thirty days.
and the firstborn that she will bear. And the continuation of the verse: "shall rise up in the name of his dead brother."
from oral tradition. The Sages' oral tradition in the interpretation of Scripture.

the oldest of the brothers shall rise up in the name of his dead brother. The firstborn brother, that is, the eldest of the brothers, establishes a name for his deceased brother and performs yibbum with his wife (and see Hilchot Nachalot 3:7).
and what it says "that she will bear" means that the mother bore. It is interpreted as: that the mother of the deceased bore.
together with the meaning "that the yevamah will bear". The son that the yevamah bears shall rise up in the name of his dead brother, according to the plain meaning of the words (and see below 6:8).
they go around to all the brothers. They go around to the other brothers.
until the one who went comes. Another brother who went to a distant place.
the deaf-mute. Who cannot perform chalitzah (below 6:3; for the definition of a deaf-mute see Hilchot Ishut 2:26).
and they consult him. To find out whether he wants to perform yibbum.
his younger brother. The brother younger than him in years.
we say to the one who is here. For one does not delay a mitzvah (Babylonian Talmud, Yevamot 39b).
like the law of a woman who rebels against her husband. Who is divorced and loses her ketubah (for the details of this law see Hilchot Ishut 14:8-14).
his brother left many wives. The law is that one of them performs yibbum or chalitzah and thereby exempts the others (above 1:9).
they are all equal. And there is no law of precedence among them (as follows).
if she wishes to perform chalitzah, etc.. And we do not urge him to perform chalitzah immediately (as above halachah 9), since here the delay is by her choice.
she waited for him. She said she is waiting for him.
she takes her ketubah if she has a ketubah. She receives the ketubah payment, if she has a basic right to it (for some women have no ketubah; see Hilchot Ishut 10:11, 24:2-4).
afflicted with boils or has other bodily defects. For even if she were married to a husband with such a defect, a wife is not compelled to live with him (for details see ibid. 25:11-13).
his field was swept away. His field was washed away by a flood, that is, he lost his property (see ibid. halachah 4).
who vowed to derive no benefit from the yavam. Who vowed not to benefit from the yavam in any way.
we compel him to perform chalitzah for her. For she is forbidden to live with him.
she vowed after her husband's death. And it is evident that she did so because she does not wish to enter yibbum.
we ask him to perform chalitzah for her. If he is willing. And then he is obligated to pay her ketubah.
she is a rebellious wife. Who did not wish to enter yibbum, and he performs chalitzah for her and does not pay her ketubah (as above halachah 10).
unless she rebelled. And said explicitly that she does not want him.

rather I will sit in my husband's house like other widows. A widow from marriage has the right to continue living in her husband's house and being supported from his estate, as long as she wishes, until she collects her ketubah or becomes betrothed to another (Hilchot Ishut 18:1-3).
they were acquired to this one from Heaven. They were commanded by Torah law to marry.
and I will sit as an agunah all my days. She wants to remain without permission to marry others.
no one gives me a wife. The yavam claims that people refrain from marrying a woman to him because they think there is already a woman destined to marry him.
he may marry another woman. And he can claim that people refrain from giving him another woman because of the yevamah.
or he will have a quarrel in his house because of the yevamah. For his wife will fear that he will perform yibbum with her and she will have a co-wife in her house.
a yevamah who had no ketubah from her husband because she was forbidden to him. For example, by a negative prohibition or a rabbinic prohibition (explained in Hilchot Ishut 24:2-4).
as will be explained. Below 6:13.
the addition. The sum the husband added voluntarily.
who sold him her ketubah, waives it. Who received payment for it during his lifetime, or waived the ketubah without any payment.
like other widows. Whose basic sum is a hundred dinars (see Hilchot Ishut 22:14).
forbidden to marry a stranger. Another man, who is not the yavam.
and he divorces her with a get. He must divorce her with a get, because the betrothal may take effect with her (see Hilchot Ishut 4:14).
even if she had several children. Unlike other cases where, if there are children, we fear for rumors about their lineage and he need not divorce her (compare Hilchot Sotah 2:13).
and she became forbidden to him and to her yavam. Similar to a woman who thought her husband had died and married another, and her husband came (Hilchot Gerushin 10:5).
was betrothed. And has not yet married.

she leaves the stranger with a get so that the sinner not profit. For if the priest performs chalitzah for her without her being divorced, the one who betrothed her would gain from the transgression he committed - he forbade the yevamah to the priest and could continue living with her.
as we explained. Hilchot Gerushin 10:5-6.
and the yevamah who committed adultery while bound. Who committed adultery while waiting for yibbum or chalitzah.
as we explained. Above 1:5.
he performs chalitzah for her and she stays with her husband. Here we do not penalize the one who betrothed her, since this is only a rabbinic doubt.
he does not perform chalitzah for her. Rather she may remain with her priest husband.

if the priest divorced her or died, she performs chalitzah, etc.. She was permitted not to perform chalitzah because of her priest husband, but now she must perform chalitzah initially because of the doubt.

I have children - he is believed. Even though it was not known that he has any, for he is believed in testimony that permits, as long as there is no information contradicting his words (see Babylonian Talmud, Kiddushin 64b).
I have brothers - he is not believed to forbid his wife. From marrying others.
for this is aimed at forbidding her after his death. For without his words she would be permitted, since it was not known that he had brothers, and he is not believed to forbid.
it is established that he has brothers. It was publicly known that he has brothers.
he is not believed. For proof is needed to contradict the presumption.
he said of one who was presumed. Who was known to be his brother.
and a rumor went out about her. A rumor.
even though he is his son regarding inheritance. For regarding inheritance he is believed, since a person may give his property as a gift to anyone he wishes (see Hilchot Nachalot 4:1).
and he has no presumption. Unlike a child born within marriage, where there is a presumption that the children are the husband's (see Hilchot Issurei Bi'ah 15:20).

one witness is believed to testify to the yevamah that her husband died, and she may enter yibbum on his word. He testifies that the husband died, and the woman is permitted to enter yibbum with his brother even without two witnesses to the death.
that her yavam died. He testifies that her husband's brother died, and she is released from the obligation of yibbum and is permitted to marry others.
or that a son was born to her husband. That a son was born to him from another woman, and then she is exempt from yibbum and chalitzah.
even a slave or a woman or a gentile. Who are disqualified from testimony (Hilchot Edut 9:10).
speaking in the course of conversation. The information about the yavam's death was stated in the course of his talk, without intending to testify.
as we explained in Hilchot Gerushin. 12:15. They accepted a single witness to permit the wife of a man who died, to ease the situation of agunot (below halachah 11).

and the five women who do not testify for one another. Because they hate her, and there is concern that they wish to harm her and forbid her: her mother-in-law and her mother-in-law's daughter, her co-wife, her sister-in-law, and her husband's daughter (Hilchot Gerushin 7:3, 12:16).

and the law of this testimony is the law of that testimony, etc.. For all matters, the laws of testimony about the death of the yavam are the same as the laws of testimony about the death of the husband.

witnesses who contradict one another. The first witness who testifies to the yavam's death is believed as two, and if another witness later comes and says he did not die, the second is not believed (ibid. 12:18).
two yevamot, etc.. Sisters-in-law, the wives of two brothers.
this one says: my husband died, etc.. Each of them is believed regarding the death of her husband, for herself (Hilchot Gerushin 12:15).

this one is forbidden because of the husband of that one, etc.. For he is her yavam, and she is bound to him after her husband's death. And she cannot rely on the testimony of his wife that he died, because she is one of the five hating women.
as we explained. In the previous halachah.
the one who has the witness remains forbidden. From marrying another.

for she is not forbidden because of her husband but because of her yavam. Although it was testified that her husband died, she is still bound to yibbum as long as there is no other testimony that he died.
she is believed to say: my husband died. See Hilchot Gerushin 12:15.
one who has children permits. Because her husband died, and she need not enter yibbum.
if they had. The yevamot, each testifying that her husband died, who have neither witnesses nor children (above halachah 7).
another yavam. Another brother of the brothers who died.
forbidden to marry a stranger. For they became bound to yibbum again as at the beginning, and regarding each of them there is no proof that her yavam died (see Maggid Mishneh).
and it is a negative prohibition. As explained above 2:18.
lest it be light in her eyes. And she will not refrain from lying because of this prohibition, in order to be permitted to marry.

my sister died, so that she may enter his house. Because she wants to marry her sister's husband, for she is not forbidden to him as a forbidden relation if the sister died (Hilchot Issurei Bi'ah 2:9).
to permit an agunah. To ease the woman's situation, so that she not be forbidden to marry another when there are not two witnesses to the husband's death.
as we explained. Hilchot Gerushin 12:15, 13:29.
she is not believed. To exempt herself from yibbum, because when she left it was known that she had a yavam, so she is presumed bound to a yavam and forbidden to a stranger.
I had a yavam overseas and he died. She testifies that her husband had a brother, and that brother died, so she is exempt from the obligation of yibbum.
for the mouth that forbade is the mouth that permitted. Since she is forbidden only because of her own words, she is believed to permit this prohibition.
she is believed, for she was presumed permitted to a stranger. When she left she had a son, and she was presumed exempt from yibbum.
my son died and afterward my husband died. And she is bound to yibbum, for when her husband died he had no sons.
she is not believed to enter yibbum. For her words are against the original presumption.
and afterward my husband died. And according to her words she is obligated in yibbum.
she is believed and enters yibbum. For originally she was presumed permitted for yibbum.
and we are concerned for her words, etc.. That perhaps she is forbidden to enter yibbum, since according to her words she is exempt from yibbum, and therefore she performs chalitzah.
in what case is this said. That she performs chalitzah because of the presumption, although she says she is permitted without it.
who was a divorcee or a chalalah. Who are forbidden to marry a priest (Hilchot Issurei Bi'ah 17:1), so the chalitzah does not add a prohibition on her regarding the priesthood.
in a cave, meaning when they died. That only she was present at their death, and there is no concern that witnesses will come.
and this chalitzah turns out to be nothing. It is not considered chalitzah, and as a result they would permit her to marry a priest.
and it would seem that a chalutzah is permitted to a priest. An observer might think so, but in truth she is forbidden to the priesthood by rabbinic enactment (ibid. 17:7).
she remains presumed bound as when she left. As she was when she left, when it was not known that she had children.
whose husband went with her co-wife. He went abroad with his other wife, and children may have been born to them there.
and it turns out it was not chalitzah. For she was exempt from yibbum, because a son was born to the deceased.
by witnesses who came. Who testified that a son was born to the co-wife.
she waits ninety days like other yevamot. To determine whether she herself is pregnant (above 1:19).

and she need not worry about her co-wife, since her husband was not with her in the country. She need not wait at all because of the co-wife, since there is no concern that she is pregnant when she lives apart from her husband (and see Orah VeSimchah).
and she had a mother-in-law overseas. The husband's mother was abroad, and she may have given birth to a son who is the husband's brother.
she need not worry that her mother-in-law gave birth... rather we leave her in her presumption. That her husband has no brothers.
her mother-in-law left pregnant. When the mother-in-law went overseas she was pregnant, and thus the presumption that the husband has no brothers is impaired.
your husband died and afterward your son died. And according to their testimony she need not enter yibbum.
that the matters were reversed. That her son died first and afterward her husband died, and she was bound to yibbum or chalitzah, and was forbidden to marry a stranger.
she leaves and the child is fit. She must be divorced from her second husband with a get (as above 2:18), and the child is not a mamzer, since this is only a negative prohibition.
your son died and afterward your husband died. And she is obligated in yibbum.
and the child who was born... is a mamzer. Who was born of a brother's wife for whom there is no mitzvah of yibbum, who is forbidden as a forbidden relation (Hilchot Issurei Bi'ah 2:1).
to the place where he is. To the city where he is.
and they call him. To come to the court.
and they give him advice suitable for him and for her. They counsel him to choose the best option for both.
for example, she is young and he is old, etc.. For such matches do not work well (see Hilchot Issurei Bi'ah 21:26).
to fix a place where they will sit. To decide in advance to sit together in a particular place.
and his yevamah went up to the gate. The yevamah came to the place where the judges sit.
they happened to be there, and she and he were before them. The judges, the yevamah and the yavam happened to be in the same place.

to be read to. That they properly recite the text they will say at the chalitzah ceremony: she says, "My brother-in-law refuses to establish a name for his brother in Israel; he does not wish to perform yibbum with me," and he says, "I do not wish to take her" (below halachah 6).
until they are fluent. Accustomed to this reading.
so that her words not sound like "my yavam is willing". If she errs in the punctuation of the words, it would sound as if she said that he is willing to marry her.
she cannot. To read the words in one breath.
by day. Because chalitzah is like the start of a legal proceeding, and a proceeding is begun only by day, not at night (Babylonian Talmud, Yevamot 104b; and see Hilchot Sanhedrin 3:3).
and before three who know how to prompt, it is valid. It is enough that they know how to prompt the yavam and the yevamah what they must say; they need not be expert judges.
a convert is disqualified, etc.. For it says, "and his name shall be called in Israel," excluding converts.
and those two. In addition to the three main judges.
a shoe... that has a heel. A sole with a part that also covers the sides of the heel (and see below halachah 18).
and it is not sewn with flax. Its parts are not sewn to one another with flax threads, but it is all of leather without a mixture of another material.
and he puts it on his right. He puts the shoe on his right foot.
and plants his foot on the ground. Sets it on the ground.
and she extends her hand in court. She reaches out her hands in the sight of the judges.
and once most of the heel has slipped off. Once most of the shoe covering the heel has been removed from the foot.
and spits on the ground in front of him. In front of his face.

and afterward he prompts her, etc.. The yevamah must say: "So shall it be done to the man who does not build up his brother's house. And his name shall be called in Israel, the house of him who had his shoe removed."
thus, in this language. From the word "thus" they learned that these words must be said specifically in the language of the Torah and not in any other form.
and all those sitting there answer after her, etc.. To fulfill what is said, "and his name shall be called in Israel."
and they perform these acts for their sake. For the sake of permitting the woman to marry a stranger (see below halachot 24-25).
and the blind man. A blind person.
or that she recited. The declaration: "So shall it be done to the man..."
why should she not return and spit in order. So that the spitting will come after the chalitzah.

lest they say that spitting alone is nothing. If she has to spit a second time, observers might think the first spit was meaningless, whereas by law spitting alone is like an invalid chalitzah, which forbids the yevamah from entering yibbum with any of the other brothers (below halachot 14, 26).
her chalitzah is valid. Because the Torah was particular only about an act done to the man's body (Mishnah Yevamot 12:3).
their chalitzah is invalid... they did nothing. For the difference between the terms see below halachah 26.

for they are fit to be read to. Then the reading is not essential. But if from the outset it is impossible to fulfill the mitzvah properly, they are disqualified from chalitzah (for another example of this principle see Hilchot Ma'aseh HaKorbanot 17:6).
"So shall be done to the man" - the act is what is effective. Only the physical acts count in chalitzah, not the recitation, which is not an act.
does not hold up the chalitzah. If it was not done (as above halachah 12).
and does not help. It does not disqualify if it was done.
and they sit. Whereas initially they should stand (above halachah 7).
on his shin from the knee down. Below the knee. And initially one should tie the shoe on the top of the foot (see above halachah 6).
who do not know how to prompt. Whereas initially they must know how to prompt (ibid.).
the blind man who performed chalitzah. Although initially he does not perform it (above halachah 8).
at night. For chalitzah must be performed by day (above halachah 5).
before two. For chalitzah must be performed before three (ibid.).

and one of them was found to be a relative or disqualified. It was discovered that one of the judges is a relative of the yavam or yevamah, or of another judge, and is disqualified for this judgment (for more see Hilchot Edut chapter 13). Likewise if he was found disqualified to judge for another reason, such as being a transgressor (ibid. 9:1).
that he untied. The knot. And she must do this (above halachah 6).
and she removed it. She took the shoe off the foot.
she intended and he did not intend. For chalitzah requires intention (above halachah 8).
before an individual. One judge.
a deaf-mute, an insane person, and a minor. Who lack understanding (below 6:3; for the definition of deaf-mute and minor see Hilchot Ishut chapter 2).
one who is exempt from chalitzah and from yibbum. Who is not obligated in yibbum and chalitzah at all.
is not chalitzah. It has no effect of chalitzah at all (see below halachah 26).
his foot is twisted backward. And when he walks he steps on the top of his foot.
turned over on its side. His foot is twisted inward, and he steps on the side of his foot.
to plant his heel on the ground. To place his foot on the ground straight.
with a shoe of cloth. Made of fabric.
hair. Goat hair.
fiber. A kind of thin netting that grows around the date palm.
cork. The bark of the oak.
covering. A cover.
was worn through. The sole was worn away.
its bottom. Its sole.
and its sides. The sides of the shoe.
that the shoe was large enough to walk in. The shoe is larger than his foot, but he can walk in it.
the quarantined or the confirmed. A sandal afflicted with tzara'at, which was quarantined to determine its impurity, or declared definitely impure and must be burned (Hilchot Tum'at Tzara'at 12:1).
the image. The likeness of an idol.
she may not perform chalitzah with it. They are repulsive for the performance of the mitzvah.
her chalitzah is valid even though it is forbidden for benefit. For performing a mitzvah is not considered benefit (see Hilchot Shofar 1:3).
offered to idolatry. Brought as a gift and offering to an idol.
an apostate city. Where most of the inhabitants were enticed to worship idols, whose law is that the city and all its property are burned in fire (Hilchot Avodah Zarah chapter 4).

for it is not meant for walking. A sandal made for a corpse is not intended for walking, and likewise idolatrous sandals and those of an apostate city, whose law is to be burned (Yad Peshutah). A confirmed-impure sandal also must be burned, but chalitzah with it is valid, because with tzara'at the Torah extended the rule so that it counts as a vessel even at the time of its burning (see Babylonian Talmud, Yevamot 103b).
and the gargir. A sharp edible vegetable.
that cause saliva to flow. That cause saliva to drip.
is nothing. It is not spitting.
flowing. Flowing.
if she sucked. The blood.
flecks of saliva. Drops of saliva.
and the wind caught it. Blew it away.
she was tall and he was short. She is tall and he is short.
a chalitzah by mistake is invalid. A chalitzah done by misleading the one performing it. For chalitzah must be done specifically for the sake of permitting the woman (above halachah 16).
perform chalitzah for her and thereby you take her in marriage. Perform chalitzah for this yevamah, and through this act you marry her.
a declaration of protest. Advance notice to witnesses that a certain act a person is about to perform is done against his will and is therefore not valid (for an example see Hilchot Mechirah 10:1).
to cancel the declaration as is done with a get. He cancels everything he said that invalidates the get (see Hilchot Gerushin 6:20).
his chalitzah is valid. For his true will is to fulfill the commandments, and therefore the chalitzah is considered to have been done willingly (see ibid. 2:20).
laymen. Who did not know the law.
forced him on their own. They coerced him, not as agents of the Jewish court.
and did not disqualify her from the priesthood. She is permitted to marry a priest.
her chalitzah is invalid, etc.. We are strict with it as if it were a valid chalitzah.
her relatives are forbidden to him. As explained above 1:13.
and she is forbidden to the brothers. As explained there, halachah 12.
she transgressed and married... and we do not remove her from him. Unlike the case where she married without any chalitzah, where we remove her if she married another (above 2:18).
and she is disqualified for them. Even though she did not perform chalitzah before a court (see above halachah 16).
perhaps she intended chalitzah. Since this act is unusual, there is concern that she did it for the sake of chalitzah (Yad Peshutah).

a court record, so that she has proof that she performed chalitzah. A confirmation by the court of a proceeding that took place. Unlike other documents, where the document itself has meaning and force, such as a get or a debt document.
unless they know. The yavam and yevamah.

for the judges, etc.. And therefore one can rely on their actions (for a similar halachah regarding mi'un see Hilchot Gerushin 11:10). But in other documents the writer must know the parties (see Hilchot Gerushin 2:3, Hilchot Mechirah 24:3).

Translation of the text of the chalitzah document:. On such-and-such a day, such-and-such a date of the month of so-and-so, in the year so-and-so by the reckoning we are accustomed to use in such-and-such a place, we, the judges, some of whom are signed below, were sitting as a court of three together. And there came before us So-and-so daughter of So-and-so, widow of So-and-so, and brought before us a man named So-and-so son of So-and-so. And this So-and-so said to us: "This So-and-so son of So-and-so is the brother of So-and-so from his father, to whom I was married, and he died, and left no living child, neither son nor daughter, to inherit and establish a name in Israel. And this So-and-so, his brother, is fit to perform yibbum with me. Now the Sages told him: if he wishes to perform yibbum with me, let him do so; and if not, let him extend his right foot before you, and I will remove his shoe from his foot and spit in his face." And we recognized that this So-and-so is the brother of the deceased So-and-so from his father, and we said to him: "If you wish to perform yibbum with her, do so; and if not, extend your right foot before us, and she will remove your shoe from your foot and spit in your face." And he answered and said: "I do not wish to perform yibbum with her." Immediately we prompted this So-and-so: "My brother-in-law refuses to establish a name for his brother in Israel; he does not wish to perform yibbum with me." And we also prompted this So-and-so: "I do not wish to take her." And he extended his right foot to her, and she removed his shoe from his foot, and spat in his face spittle that we saw from her mouth on the ground. And again we prompted her: "So shall it be done to the man who does not build up his brother's house. And his name shall be called in Israel, the house of him who had his shoe removed." And we the judges and all who were sitting before us answered after her: "The one whose shoe was removed, the one whose shoe was removed, the one whose shoe was removed," three times. And once this act was done before us, we permitted this So-and-so to go and marry whomever she wishes, and no one shall protest against her from this day forever. And this So-and-so requested of us this document of chalitzah, and we wrote, signed and gave it to her as her right, in accordance with the law of Moses and Israel.
and three testify to it. Judges.
or two of the three. Therefore they write in the document, "some of us are signed below."
as we explained. Above halachah 29.
and likewise in other Torah testimony. In a case where the testimony concerns something that is bound to become known.
testimony about a prohibition. Testimony on matters of prohibited and permitted, such as the kashrut of foods.
at the end of Hilchot Gerushin. 13:29.
as we have informed. Above 2:1-2.

Translation of the text of the yevamin ketubah:. On such-and-such a day... So-and-so son of So-and-so came before us, and So-and-so son of So-and-so said to us: "My brother from my father died, and left no living child, neither son nor daughter, to inherit and establish a name in Israel. And he left that woman named So-and-so daughter of So-and-so, and she is fit for me by the Torah to perform yibbum with her, as is written in the Book of the Torah of Moses: 'her yavam shall come to her.' And this So-and-so agreed, and entered yibbum with So-and-so the yavam, to establish a name in Israel, as it is written: 'And the firstborn that she bears shall rise up in the name of his dead brother, so that his name not be erased from Israel.' And So-and-so the yavam wrote to So-and-so his yevamah two hundred silver zuzim that are due her, which were written in her ketubah that her first husband wrote for her, and added from his own such-and-such. And this is the dowry she brought in to him, etc.

Translation of the form of the ketubah:. On such-and-such a day... that So-and-so son of So-and-so said to So-and-so daughter of So-and-so, the virgin bride: "Be my wife according to the law of Moses and Israel, and I, by the word of the Lord, will work for you, honor you, support you, feed you, provide for you and clothe you, in the manner of Jewish men who work, honor, support, feed, provide for and clothe their wives faithfully. And I give you the mohar of your virginity, two hundred silver zuzim, which are twenty-five zuzim of pure silver, that are due you, and your food, clothing and needs, and to come to you as is the way of all the earth." And this So-and-so agreed, and became his wife. And he agreed and added to her an addition to the principal of the ketubah, up to a total of such-and-such. And this is the dowry she brought in to him, such-and-such; all of it this groom received, and it came into his hand and into his possession, and he assumed responsibility for it all as a loan and debt. And this groom said to us: "The responsibility for this entire ketubah, principal, dowry and addition, along with the other ketubah conditions, I have taken upon myself and upon my heirs after me, and upon every best and choicest of property and acquisition I have under all the heavens, that I have acquired and will acquire, land and movables and movables attached to land - all of them shall be responsible and bound for this entire ketubah, principal, dowry and addition, to be collected from them in my lifetime and after my death, even from the cloak on my shoulders." And we effected a complete acquisition from this So-and-so for all that is written and explained above, not as an asmachta and not as a mere form of documents, but... and everything is clear, firm and confirmed.
almanta. Widow. He writes this because the amount of her ketubah is different, as mentioned below.
so that a priest not stumble with her. Who is forbidden to marry a divorcee or a captive (Hilchot Issurei Bi'ah 18:17).

and I give you, etc.. "And I give you your mohar, one hundred silver zuzim, which are twelve and a half zuzim of pure silver, that are due you." A hundred zuz is the ketubah of a woman who is not a virgin (Hilchot Ishut 10:7-8).
yevamin document. A chalitzah document.
ruled. Draws lines so that the letters are straight, as is done with sacred writings (Hilchot Sefer Torah 7:16).
for it is forbidden to write three words without ruling. In non-sacred documents (Yad Peshutah).
until she completes ninety days. Lest she be pregnant (above 1:19).
that the yavam gave her a get. Before he took her in yibbum.
disqualified her. She is thereby forbidden to enter yibbum with him or with his brother (above 1:12).
by their enactment, since a get divorces a married woman. Because it severs a marriage bond elsewhere, the Sages enacted that it does so in yibbum too, as a stringency.
a get that disqualifies his wife from the priesthood. Even if the get is not a complete get (see Hilchot Gerushin 10:1).
the ma'amar. Betrothal of a yevamah by rabbinic enactment (above 2:1).
she needs a get from him. To cancel the bond created by the ma'amar.
and she is permitted to a stranger only through chalitzah. For she still needs chalitzah as at the beginning.
for the yevamah is not permitted to a stranger, etc.. For only relations or chalitzah completely remove the bond of yibbum from her.
and he gave a get for his ma'amar. He specified that the get was meant to cancel the ma'amar he made.
and permitted her. To enter yibbum.
to her bond. To cancel the bond of yibbum between them.
as we explained. Above halachah 1.
unless he had relations. Who made a ma'amar and had relations afterward.
from another yavam. His brother.
an invalid ma'amar. And she needs a get to remove its prohibition (below halachot 11, 13).
that came after it. That the acts mentioned took place after the ma'amar.
or relations. With the co-wife.
invalid relations. And she needs a get and chalitzah (below halachah 11) to be permitted.

reduced chalitzah. Which permits only the woman who performed it, and not her co-wives (below halachah 12). This term is reserved for chalitzah in a place where yibbum is prohibited (see further below 7:9-10), unlike invalid chalitzah - disqualified because of other defects, which does not even permit the chalutzah herself to marry (above 4:26).
who come from one house. The widows of one brother.

and one of them needs chalitzah. One of the yevamot, and with this chalitzah all the co-wives are permitted. This chalitzah is not considered a reduced chalitzah that does not permit the co-wives, because by Torah law the relations removed the bond of yibbum (Yad Peshutah).
that she go around to all the brothers. That all of them perform chalitzah for her.
for a reduced chalitzah does not remove the bond of yibbum from this house, etc.. For the force of the chalitzah is weakened by the get or ma'amar that came before it.
for the sake of marriage. For the sake of betrothal.
for the sake of yibbum. To fulfill the mitzvah of yibbum.
as we explained. Above halachot 2-3.
for the get does not push away the yevamah completely. For a get does not permit her to marry a stranger.
effective. Valid - the ma'amar acquires and the get pushes away.
relations after relations with her... the last is of no effect. With that same woman specifically; but if he had relations with her co-wife, she needs a get (above halachah 13).
for this is like performing chalitzah for the other women, etc.. Like chalitzah for women for whom there is no mitzvah of yibbum, which has no significance.

and betrothal does not take effect with a married woman. Like all women forbidden as forbidden relations (Hilchot Ishut 4:12), and after relations this yevamah is that yavam's wife for all purposes (see above 1:1, 15).
or had relations with her co-wife, she needs a get, as we explained. Above halachah 13.
both leave with a get. For regarding one of the yevamot there is a prohibition, after her co-wife was taken in yibbum.
we do not remove her from him until it is known, etc.. We do not require him to divorce her out of doubt, as long as it is not clear that he is violating a prohibition.
nine years and one day old. Whose relations count as relations (above 1:15).

his relations are like the ma'amar of an adult, which does not acquire completely. The relations of a nine-year-old have the law of a ma'amar, which does not acquire but only disqualifies the yevamah for the other brothers (below halachah 19).
at the beginning. For his ma'amar preceded any other act with this yevamah.
at the end. After an act had already been done with the yevamah.
and his chalitzah are nothing. As above 4:16.
as we explained. Above halachot 14-15.
like the law of ma'amar and ma'amar. As above halachah 15.
she needs only a get. Like any woman for whom full yibbum took place.
and one nine years and one day and one twenty years, etc.. Their law is equal, for both are considered minors.
and the signs of a saris did not appear in him. For if they appeared and he is a saris, he is not obligated at all in yibbum and chalitzah (below 6:2).
at the beginning of the book. Hilchot Ishut 2:11.
a minor who is fit to refuse. A girl whose father died and whom her family married off, who can refuse her husband (while still a minor) and leave without a get (Hilchot Gerushin 11:1).
as we explained. Hilchot Ishut 4:8-9.
and her betrothal is suspended until she grows up. And after she grows up she becomes a fully married woman (ibid. 4:8).

and for a deaf-mute woman they enacted marriage so that she not remain unmarried forever. So that she can marry although she lacks understanding. Her marriage is always rabbinic, whereas for the minor, once she grows up, the marriage becomes Torah-level.
the relations of one of them exempt them all. Because the deficiency in the marriage of all of them is the same.
and how is their remedy. For they cannot perform chalitzah (above 4:13, 4:16).
we teach the minor to refuse. We instruct her to refuse the yavam, thereby uprooting the bond between them (Hilchot Gerushin 11:3).
for her betrothal is only rabbinic. In contrast to the betrothal of a woman of sound mind, which is complete betrothal.
did not disqualify the first. For other relations disqualify only if they are of higher standing (below halachot 27-28), and here the status of both is equal.
we teach the second to refuse. And she will sever the bond to the yavam, since otherwise he may not keep her, as with invalid relations that require a get (see above halachah 13).
and the deaf-mute needs a get. As with invalid relations (above halachah 13).
disqualified the deaf-mute. For the relations of the minor are of higher standing than hers (above halachah 27).
and we teach the minor to refuse. To sever her bond with the yavam, so that the deaf-mute not be disqualified.
and the deaf-mute leaves with a get. If he wishes to divorce her (Yad Peshutah).
did not disqualify the woman of sound mind. For relations with a woman of sound mind have the law of full marriage.
with a get and chalitzah. A get, because her relations are invalid relations. And chalitzah, because the relations of the deaf-mute did not exempt her from yibbum (Yad Peshutah).
did not disqualify the adult, and we teach the minor to refuse. For this minor's relations are like invalid relations.
and we teach the minor to refuse. So that he can keep the adult.
and they have no presumption at all. They are not obligated in the mitzvah of yibbum and chalitzah.
a saris chamah. A person whose sexual development is impaired and who cannot father children (for his signs see Hilchot Ishut 2:13).
and an androgynos. One born with both male and female organs (ibid. halachot 24-25).
and they never had a time of fitness. They were never fit to father children.
because they have no understanding to perform chalitzah. But for yibbum no understanding is needed, and the intention to have relations suffices (above 2:3-4).

and when a deaf-mute performs yibbum, he never divorces, etc.. Because she became his wife by force of the marriage of his hearing brother, whose betrothal was complete. He, however, can divorce only from marriages that are rabbinic (Hilchot Gerushin 2:17).
as we explained. Above 5:18.
a doubtful forbidden relation. A doubtful incest prohibition on the yavam (see below halachah 13).
and one with crushed testicles. Whose testicles were crushed.
and one whose organ was cut. Whose male organ or part of it was cut off (for the full definition see Hilchot Issurei Bi'ah 16:3-9).
whose strength weakened and failed. Who is unable to have relations.
a man-made saris. Who was castrated by a person, including one with crushed testicles and one whose organ was cut (Hilchot Ishut 2:14).
for he had a time of fitness. He was fit for relations before he was castrated.
for he is forbidden to enter the congregation. For one with crushed testicles or a cut organ is forbidden to marry a fit Israelite woman (Hilchot Issurei Bi'ah 16:1).
and the tumtum. One whose sexual organs are covered within his body, and it is not known whether he is male or female (Hilchot Ishut 2:25).
because it is a doubt. Perhaps he is male.
to read and understand. To read the text of the chalitzah and understand the act of chalitzah (above 4:3-4).
he divorces. Because a woman can be divorced even against her will (Hilchot Gerushin 1:2).
those forbidden by negative prohibitions. Whose relations the Torah forbade in the language of a negative prohibition and which carry no karet, such as a mamzeret to an Israelite (Hilchot Ishut 1:7).
and secondary relations. Those forbidden by rabbinic enactment.
and those forbidden by positive commandments. Whose relations are forbidden in the Torah in the language of a positive commandment (ibid. 1:8).
as will be explained. Below halachah 10.

for there is nothing to be concerned about here. For if she was betrothed to his brother, he is now fulfilling the mitzvah of yibbum, and if not, he is permitted to marry her, because she was never his brother's wife.
they had a time of fitness. They were fit to bear children.
and an ailonit. A woman whose sexual development is impaired and who does not bear children (for her signs see Hilchot Ishut 2:6).
whose name is erased. Who have no continuation of generations.
because they have no marriage at all. She is not considered married to them.
for he has no acquisition in her. Betrothal does not take effect with her (ibid. 4:12).
and by law they should have entered yibbum. That would have been correct in principle.
therefore. Because they are bound to yibbum and betrothal takes effect with them.
and needless to say the second. Whose prohibition is only rabbinic.
he has made a complete acquisition, etc.. As if she were a fit yevamah.
for she is a widow from marriage. Who married a regular priest who died, and fell to yibbum before her husband's brother, who is a high priest.

a prohibition and a positive commandment. That apply to a high priest: the prohibition is that of a widow, and the positive commandment is to marry a virgin (Hilchot Ishut 1:7-8, Hilchot Issurei Bi'ah 17:1, 17:13).
this is not his wife. She is not considered the wife of the deceased brother (Hilchot Ishut 4:12).
he may marry her and perform yibbum with her co-wife, he has permission. Since in truth the forbidden relation was not the deceased's wife, there is no prohibition against marrying two yevamot.
except for one who remarries his divorcee after she married, etc.. Who is forbidden to her husband by a negative prohibition (Hilchot Gerushin 11:12).

or a doubtful forbidden relation to her husband, she performs chalitzah and does not enter yibbum. Some explained that this law applies only where he betrothed one of two sisters, for the doubtful incest of the husband also affects the fulfillment of yibbum - just as the husband cannot marry either of them, lest she be his wife's sister (a doubtful forbidden relation), so too the yavam cannot perform yibbum with either, lest she be the sister of the woman bound to him (Migdal Oz). But in a case of another doubtful forbidden relation on the husband but not on the yavam, he can perform yibbum with her, for if she is not a forbidden relation, he is performing proper yibbum, and if she is forbidden, she is not his brother's wife at all and he may marry her.
who married her sister. Who is already married to her sister.
because she is a doubtful forbidden relation. For if there was betrothal, she is the sister of his betrothed.
because she is doubtfully a relative of his chalutzah. For if there was no betrothal, she is the sister of his chalutzah.
as we explained. Above 1:13.
for he has acquisition in whichever of them he wishes. For he can perform yibbum with any of the women.
a forbidden relation to him as his brother's wife. Like any brother's wife who has no bond of yibbum (see Hilchot Issurei Bi'ah 2:1).
because she was the co-wife of a forbidden relation. Of Reuven's wife, when she fell before Shimon for yibbum.

and the same law applies to the co-wife of her co-wife until the end of the world. For if this co-wife of Shimon is taken in yibbum by another brother, she forbids her new co-wife to Shimon as well. And so on.
his brother who was not in his world. Who was born only after his brother died.
until both of them were in the world. That they be alive at the same time.
whether he was born before Shimon performed yibbum. And was born in a situation where she is bound to a yavam, and apparently he cannot perform yibbum with her because of a scriptural decree.

or born after he performed yibbum with her. For even if Levi was born after Reuven's wife entered yibbum with Shimon, she is not considered Shimon's wife for all purposes in this matter, and she is forbidden to enter yibbum with Levi.
that he marry. Through relations, as is the law of yibbum.
performs chalitzah for her co-wife. For she is not considered the co-wife of a brother's wife who was not in his world at all.
as we explained. Above 2:1, 5:2.
willingly and with witnesses. Is forbidden to her husband (Hilchot Gerushin 11:14).

for "impurity" is written regarding her as with forbidden relations. The term "impurity" is mentioned in the prohibitions of incest: "do not defile yourselves with any of these" (Leviticus 18:24), and a woman who committed adultery against her husband is equated with a forbidden relation regarding yibbum, and is exempt.
a sotah. Where it is not known for certain that she became impure, but she must be tested with the bitter waters (see Hilchot Sotah 3:8-10).
a sotah whose husband died before he gave her the bitter water to drink. She does not drink (ibid. 2:7).
who is not capable of drinking. Who cannot be tested with the bitter waters, and he is obligated to divorce her (ibid. 2:2).

one who performed chalitzah for his yevamah, and her sister or her mother went, etc.. They are forbidden to the one who performed chalitzah by rabbinic enactment, for the Sages decreed to forbid the relatives of a chalutzah as for a divorcee (above 1:13).

because she is confused with the co-wife of his chalutzah. Although this is a co-wife of a secondary prohibition, she is forbidden out of concern that people will not distinguish between the chalutzah and her relative, and will come to permit even the chalutzah's co-wife.
she refused him. While she was a minor.
at the time of falling to yibbum. At the time of the brother's death.
betrothed to his brother who died in doubt, etc.. Since the marriage is not complete, the forbidden relation does not exempt.

even though she refused the yavam, etc.. Although refusing the yavam uproots the marriage bond from its root, the co-wife is not permitted to him, since at the time of death the co-wife appeared to be the co-wife of a forbidden relation (and see Hilchot Gerushin 11:17).
the forbidden relation turned out to be an ailonit. And it was discovered afterward that the co-wife was in fact bound to yibbum or chalitzah (see above halachah 21).

the co-wife leaves her husband and her yavam. She leaves her husband because she married him in violation of a prohibition, and she became forbidden to her yavam when she married another (above 2:18).
to permit her to the market. To marry others.
they thought. They thought.

she leaves her yavam with a get. Lest people say that his brother divorced the forbidden relation shortly before his death, and the co-wife properly entered yibbum, and it would turn out that a married woman leaves her husband without a get (Orah VeSimchah).
and the child is a mamzer. For the co-wife is forbidden to him as a brother's wife (above halachah 14).
a stranger. Who is not a relative of the other wives.

in the bond of the brother who died last. The bond is a relationship of marriage-kinship between the yevamah and the brother of the deceased. This bond makes the unrelated woman a kind of co-wife of the yavam's wife; if the yavam died and his wife fell before the one married to her sister, she is forbidden as a wife's sister, and the unrelated wife of the first is also forbidden as her co-wife in the bond.
the co-wife of his wife's sister in the bond for one moment. She was in this situation for a short time, from her husband's death and her falling to yibbum until the brother divorced her sister.
they did not decree this. To forbid the co-wife of a forbidden relation after the forbidden relation was divorced.
as we explained. Above halachah 21.
known to all. Because it is from the Torah (above halachah 14).
and both fell. The wife of the second and the woman of the ma'amar.
